description: VN superlative is the single particle 'nhất'; learners double-mark it as analytic 'most' + synthetic '-est'. Drops 'most' before a closed -est whitelist (tallest, biggest, fastest, …), keeping the synthetic superlative (a preceding 'the' stays). Re-capitalizes when the match is sentence-initial.
fp_risk_note: Low risk. Fires only before a fixed -est whitelist where 'most …-est' is ungrammatical. Analytic superlatives that REQUIRE 'most' ('the most beautiful', 'the most important thing'), 'most' + noun ('most people'), an already-correct synthetic superlative ('the tallest'), and 'almost' (the \bmost\b word boundary excludes it) all abstain — the negatives stress each surface, including the 'almost' boundary.

positive.notes: Double-marked superlative drops 'most'; the preceding 'the' is kept.

positive.input: It is the most biggest city
positive.notes: Mid-sentence, attributive — only 'most' removed, head noun preserved.

positive.input: I want the most fastest car
positive.notes: Mid-sentence double superlative, no re-capitalization needed.
Sentence-initial match — the new first letter is re-capitalized ('Most biggest' -> 'Biggest').

negative.notes: Analytic superlative — 'most beautiful' is correct; 'beautifulest' does not exist; not on the -est whitelist.
Already-correct synthetic superlative with no 'most' — nothing to drop.
Analytic superlative that must keep 'most'; 'important' not on the -est whitelist.
Word-boundary guard: \bmost\b must NOT match inside 'almost' — abstain.
